title: Lancashire Hotpot
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb under a crisp potato lid
excerpt: Layers of lamb neck fillet and onion slow-braised in stock, topped with thinly sliced potato that crisps in the oven. A Lancashire classic that improves with a day in the fridge.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lancashire hotpot is one of Britain's most celebrated regional dishes, from the cotton-mill towns of Lancashire where it was left in the oven all day while workers were at the mill. The original contained oysters as cheap filler protein, though this fell away as oysters became expensive. The defining feature is the tightly overlapping potato lid that becomes crisp on top while the underneath absorbs the braising juices. Lamb neck fillet is the traditional cut: it braises to tenderness without drying out.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 2-litre casserole or deep roasting tin with a lid.

content.text: Brown the lamb well before layering: a good crust adds depth to the braising liquid. Slice the potatoes for the lid very thinly and overlap them tightly so they form an even, sealed crust. Remove the lid for the last 30 minutes so the potatoes crisp properly.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Season the lamb pieces with salt and pepper, then dust with the flour. Heat the oil in a heavy casserole over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, fry the onion and carrot over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened. Return the lamb. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Arrange the sliced potatoes in overlapping circles on top to form a tight lid. Season the potato layer with salt and pepper. Dot with butter. Cover and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake for a further 30 minutes until the potato top is golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
